verdict.rationale: Appwrite's own docs say its managed databases come "with permissions and realtime" and offer a way to "respond to server events in realtime". Its auth docs also describe broadcasting presence status in realtime, and a community question about scaling its WebSocket connection pool implies a socket-based realtime layer. Even so, the evidence is a few one-line marketing claims rather than documentation of the subscription mechanism itself. missing for 10: documented client-SDK subscribe API for database row changes, channel/event granularity details, hands-on or independent confirmation that UIs update live without polling.
